cards.explanation: The answer is the land of the Philistines. David says, "There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines." I think he figures Saul, who has been searching for him, won't follow him there. Running to the Philistines is a bold move, friends, because the Philistines are gathering to fight Israel later in this very passage.

The other wife is Abigail the widow of Nabal. The text says David had "…his two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal." Two wives, six hundred men, and all their families, friends. That's one big moving day.

The answer is True. The text says that when Saul learned David had fled to Gath, "…he no longer searched for him." Remember, David had said that if he escaped, Saul would stop searching all over Israel. Well, friends, it worked out just like he said.

The reason is that a servant shouldn't live in the royal city with the king. David asks Achish, "For why should your servant live in the royal city with you?" He calls himself Achish's servant, so he asks for a town of his own. I think that's a smooth way to get some elbow room, bakers.

David takes livestock and clothing. The text says he "…took the flocks and herds, the donkeys, camels, and clothing." So it's animals and clothes, friends. This is a heavy part of the story, and the text tells it plainly.

The answer is False. The text says David and his men raided the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites. But when Achish asked, David answered, "The Negev of Judah…" or "The Negev of Jerahmeel…" or "The Negev of the Kenites." Those names are different from the peoples the text says he raided, bakers.

The word is "report." David says, "Otherwise they will report us, saying, ‘This is what David did.’…" He didn't want word getting back to Gath, friends. And the text says that was his custom the whole time he lived in Philistine territory.

The answer is False. The text says, "So Achish trusted David…" He thought, "Since he has made himself an utter stench to his people Israel, he will be my servant forever." So he never smelled anything fishy, bakers. Well, except the stench he thought David had with Israel.

Achish tells David that he and his men will go to battle with him. Achish says, "You must understand that you and your men are to go out to battle with me." The Philistines are gathering to fight Israel, friends. Achish talks like David is already on his side.

The word is "bodyguard." David says, "Then you will come to know what your servant can do." Achish answers, "Very well… I will make you my bodyguard for life." A bodyguard stands right next to the king, bakers, so that's a big job to hand somebody.
